ch1_fundamentals.topic: Provisions of Partnership Act in Absence of Deed
ch1_fundamentals.question: A, B and C are partners in a firm. They do not have a Partnership Deed. At the end of the first year of the commencement of the firm, they face the following problems: (a) A wants that interest on capital should be allowed @ 10% p.a., (b) B wants that partners should be allowed salary @ ₹ 2,000 per month, (c) C wants that interest on partner loan of ₹ 50,000 given by him should be allowed @ 10% p.a. How will you settle these disputes?
solution_steps: Applicable Law: In the absence of a Partnership Deed, the provisions of the Indian Partnership Act, 1932 apply:
(a) Interest on Capital: Not allowed. A's claim is rejected.
(b) Partners' Salary: No partner is entitled to any salary or commission. B's claim is rejected.
(c) Interest on Partner's Loan: Allowed strictly @ 6% p.a. (Section 13(d)). C's claim for 10% is rejected; he will receive 6% p.a. (₹ 3,000).
(d) Sharing of Profit/Loss: Must be shared equally irrespective of capital contributed.
ch1_fundamentals.working_notes: Section 13 of the Indian Partnership Act, 1932 governs all matters when no deed exists or deed is silent.

ch1_fundamentals.topic: Profit & Loss Appropriation Account & Capital Distribution
ch1_fundamentals.question: Anubha and Kajal are partners sharing profits in 2:1. Their capitals were ₹ 90,000 and ₹ 60,000. Interest on capital is allowed @ 5% p.a. Interest on drawings is charged @ 5% p.a. (Drawings: Anubha ₹ 8,500, Kajal ₹ 6,500). Net profit for the year before adjustments was ₹ 45,000. Prepare Profit & Loss Appropriation Account.
solution_steps: 2. Calculate Interest on Drawings @ 5% for average 6 months (no date of withdrawal given).
3. Determine Divisible Profit and distribute in 2:1 ratio.
ch1_fundamentals.working_notes:
• Interest on Capital: Anubha = ₹ 90,000 × 5% = ₹ 4,500 | Kajal = ₹ 60,000 × 5% = ₹ 3,000 (Total = ₹ 7,500)
• Interest on Drawings (Average 6 months): Anubha = 8,500 × 5% × 6/12 = ₹ 213 | Kajal = 6,500 × 5% × 6/12 = ₹ 163 (Total = ₹ 376)
• Divisible Profit = ₹ 45,000 + ₹ 376 − ₹ 7,500 = ₹ 37,876
• Anubha's Share = 37,876 × 2/3 = ₹ 25,251 | Kajal's Share = 37,876 × 1/3 = ₹ 12,625

ch1_fundamentals.topic: Interest on Monthly Drawings (Beginning, Middle, End)
ch1_fundamentals.question: A, B and C are partners. Calculate Interest on Drawings @ 10% p.a. for the year ended 31st March: (a) If A withdrew ₹ 2,000 per month in the beginning of every month, (b) If B withdrew ₹ 2,000 per month in the middle of every month, (c) If C withdrew ₹ 2,000 per month at the end of every month.
solution_steps: Total Drawings for each partner = ₹ 2,000 × 12 = ₹ 24,000 per year.
ch1_fundamentals.working_notes:
Case (a) Beginning of every month:
Average Period = (12 + 1) / 2 = 6.5 months.
Interest = 24,000 × 10/100 × 6.5/12 = ₹ 1,300

Case (b) Middle of every month:
Average Period = 6.0 months.
Interest = 24,000 × 10/100 × 6/12 = ₹ 1,200

Case (c) End of every month:
Average Period = (11 + 0) / 2 = 5.5 months.
Interest = 24,000 × 10/100 × 5.5/12 = ₹ 1,100

ch3_admission.question: X and Y are partners sharing profits and losses in 3:2. They admit Z into partnership for 1/4th share in profits, which he acquires equally from X and Y. Z brings ₹ 50,000 for capital and ₹ 20,000 for his share of goodwill in cash. Give Journal Entries and calculate New Profit Sharing Ratio.
solution_steps: 1. Calculate share sacrificed by X and Y.
2. Calculate New Profit Sharing Ratio = Old Share − Sacrificed Share.
3. Pass Journal Entries for Cash brought in and distribution of Premium for Goodwill to sacrificing partners in sacrificing ratio (1:1).
ch3_admission.working_notes:
• Share acquired from X = 1/4 × 1/2 = 1/8
• Share acquired from Y = 1/4 × 1/2 = 1/8
• Sacrificing Ratio of X and Y = 1/8 : 1/8 = 1 : 1
• X's New Share = 3/5 − 1/8 = (24 − 5)/40 = 19/40
• Y's New Share = 2/5 − 1/8 = (16 − 5)/40 = 11/40
• Z's Share = 1/4 = 10/40
• New Profit Sharing Ratio = 19 : 11 : 10

ch2_fundamentals.question: In the absence of a Partnership Deed, state the rules regarding: (a) Salaries of partners, (b) Interest on partner's capital, (c) Interest on partner's loan, (d) Division of profits.
solution_steps: As per the Indian Partnership Act, 1932 provisions:
• (a) No salary is payable to any partner.
• (b) No interest is allowed on capitals.
• (c) Interest on loan is paid @ 6% p.a.
• (d) Profits and losses are shared equally (1:1).
ch2_fundamentals.working_notes: Statutory rule: Section 13 of Indian Partnership Act 1932.
